executive_summary: A comprehensive API security assessment of the VAmPI application was conducted, evaluating 10 discovered endpoints against the OWASP API Security Top 10 framework. The evaluation revealed a severely compromised security posture, identifying 6 confirmed vulnerabilities—comprising two Critical, three High, and one Medium severity finding. The most severe threats involve a Critical Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) flaw on the password modification endpoint (CVSS 9.3) and a Critical Mass Assignment vulnerability during user registration (CVSS 9.1), which together enable unauthorized password overrides and arbitrary privilege escalation. Furthermore, High-severity access control and authentication weaknesses allow unauthenticated access to private user records, sensitive data leaks via a debug endpoint, and JWT token manipulation. The login interface also lacks basic rate-limiting controls, leaving the application highly susceptible to automated brute-force attacks. Collectively, these vulnerabilities expose the business to severe risks of total account takeover, administrative privilege compromise, and extensive unauthorized data exposure, requiring immediate prioritized remediation.

vulnerabilities.name: Excessive Data Exposure via debug endpoint
vulnerabilities.description: An undocumented debug endpoint returns full user records including plaintext passwords and email addresses for every user, to any unauthenticated caller.
vulnerabilities.evidence: GET /users/v1/_debug -> 200 and exposes password fields. Sample: {"users": [{"admin": false, "email": "mail1@mail.com", "password": "pass1", "username": "name1"}, {"admin": false, "email": "mail2@mail.com", "password": "pass2", "username": "name2"}, {"admin": true, "email": "admin@mail.com", "password": "pass1", "username": "admin"}, {"admin": false, "email": "qa_9d430c2a@example.com", "password": "Password123!", "username": "qa_79ba3071"}, {"admin": true, "ema
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove debug endpoints from production builds, never return password fields, and enforce authentication/authorization on all user data endpoints.

vulnerabilities.name: Weak JWT authentication configuration
vulnerabilities.description: The JWT issued at login has weaknesses that undermine authentication: HS256 (symmetric) signing - vulnerable if secret is weak/guessable.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use a strong, secret-managed signing key (or asymmetric RS256), enforce short-lived tokens with an 'exp' claim, and reject 'none'.

vulnerabilities.name: Mass Assignment allows privilege escalation at registration
vulnerabilities.description: Registration binds client-supplied fields directly to the user model, so an attacker can set admin=true and self-provision administrator privileges.
vulnerabilities.evidence: POST /users/v1/register with admin=true -> 200. GET /users/v1/admintest_d32c5e9f shows admin flag set: {"admin": true, "email": "qa_e67734b4@example.com", "password": "Password123!", "username": "admintest_d32c5e9f"}
vulnerabilities.remediation: Bind only an explicit allow-list of fields (username, password, email). Never accept privilege/role fields from client input.

vulnerabilities.name: Broken Object Level Authorization on user modification
vulnerabilities.description: An authenticated user can modify another user's object (password) because the server does not verify that the token owner matches the targeted username.
vulnerabilities.evidence: Attacker 'attacker_6820374d' token used to PUT /users/v1/victim_278de321/password -> 204; subsequent login as victim with attacker-set password succeeded.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Enforce object-level authorization: derive the target user from the authenticated token, not from the path parameter, or verify ownership before mutating.

vulnerabilities.name: Missing rate limiting on authentication
vulnerabilities.owasp_category: API4:2019 Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting
vulnerabilities.description: The login endpoint accepts unlimited authentication attempts with no throttling or account lockout, enabling brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks.
vulnerabilities.evidence: 12 consecutive failed logins all succeeded without a 429/lockout. HTTP codes observed: [200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200]
vulnerabilities.remediation: Apply per-IP and per-account rate limiting, exponential backoff, and account lockout after repeated failures.

vulnerabilities.name: Unauthenticated access to user records
vulnerabilities.description: The user-detail endpoint returns any user's record to an unauthenticated caller, enabling account enumeration and unauthorized information disclosure.
vulnerabilities.evidence: GET /users/v1/admin sent with NO Authorization header -> 200, returned: {"username": "admin", "email": "admin@mail.com"}
vulnerabilities.remediation: Require authentication and enforce function-level authorization so users can only read records they are permitted to access.
